newsitem.title: USA: Clinton asks Glickman to go to Chile on farm trade.
newsitem.headline: Clinton asks Glickman to go to Chile on farm trade.

text.p: President Clinton said Wednesday he had asked U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman to go to Chile to start a new consultative process on promoting farm trade between the two countries.
Speaking at a news conference after talks with Chilean President Eduardo Frei, Clinton said his administration remained committed to concluding a comprehensive free trade agreement with Chile.

"In that regard, I am pleased to announce that I've asked the Secretary of Agriculture, Dan Glickman, to travel to Chile to inaugurate a new consultative process to promote our agricultural trade," Clinton said.

Frei, speaking through an interpreter, said bilateral trade with the United States had undergone an explosive increase and there were senstive issues between the two countries, "especially in agricultural sectors."
He said Chile had expressed its way of thinking and ideas.
"And as the president has stated, our secretaries of agriculture will meet so as to jointly look for a solution to these problems that we believe always can emerge..." Frei said.
Chilean barriers to imports of U.S. poultry, beef, wheat and fruit were identified as key problems after a recent visit by House Agriculture Committee Chairman Bob Smith.
